checks.label: USB Debugging Enabled
checks.description: USB debugging should be disabled in production
checks.remediation: Disable USB debugging via 'settings put global adb_enabled 0' or in Developer Options.

checks.label: USB File Transfer Disabled
checks.description: Should be disabled to block unauthorized USB file access. Null means not configured (safe default).
checks.remediation: Disable USB file transfer via 'settings put global usb_mass_storage_enabled 0'.

checks.label: USB Mass Storage
checks.description: Check USB configuration mode. ADB mode is expected during audit.
checks.remediation: Set USB mode to charging-only via 'setprop sys.usb.config charging' when not auditing.

checks.label: Connected USB Devices Count
checks.description: USB device count - unexpected devices may indicate BadUSB or hardware keylogger
checks.remediation: Physically inspect and disconnect any unknown USB devices. Audit connected peripherals.

checks.label: USB Accessory Mode
checks.description: Current USB state. ADB mode is expected during audit.
checks.remediation: Switch USB state to charging-only after audit via 'setprop sys.usb.config charging'.

checks.label: MTP Enabled
checks.remediation: Disable MTP via 'settings put global mtp_enabled 0' to prevent file transfer over USB.

checks.label: Serial Device Files Exposed
checks.description: Serial interfaces exposed to userspace - may allow debug console access if physical UART connected
checks.remediation: Restrict serial device permissions or disable unused UART interfaces in the kernel config.

checks.label: GPIO Sysfs Exposed
checks.description: GPIO pins exported to userspace - apps can control hardware pins
checks.remediation: Unexport unused GPIO pins via 'echo <pin> > /sys/class/gpio/unexport' and restrict sysfs permissions.

checks.label: I2C Bus Exposed
checks.description: I2C bus accessible from userspace - can communicate with sensors/peripherals
checks.remediation: Restrict /dev/i2c-* permissions to root or remove kernel I2C chardev support if unused.

checks.label: SPI Bus Exposed
checks.remediation: Restrict /dev/spidev* permissions to root or disable SPI chardev support in the kernel.

checks.label: USB Gadget Controller
checks.description: USB device controller present - device can act as USB peripheral
checks.remediation: Disable USB gadget mode in kernel config if the device should not act as a USB peripheral.

checks.label: Kernel Console Enabled
checks.description: Kernel boot console configured - debug output on serial port
checks.remediation: Remove 'console=' parameters from kernel cmdline in the bootloader config for production builds.

checks.label: Video Capture Devices
checks.command: P=$(ls -d /dev/video* 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$P" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$P"; elif ls -d /dev/video* 2>&1 | grep -qi 'permission denied'; then echo UNMEASURED; else echo "ABSENT no video capture device"; fi
checks.remediation: Restrict /dev/video* permissions and disable unused camera drivers in the kernel config.

checks.label: Audio Capture Devices
checks.command: P=$(ls -d /dev/snd/pcm*c* 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$P" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$P"; elif ls -d /dev/snd/pcm*c* 2>&1 | grep -qi 'permission denied'; then echo UNMEASURED; else echo "ABSENT no audio capture device"; fi
checks.remediation: Restrict /dev/snd/ permissions and disable unused audio capture drivers if not needed.

checks.label: Raw Memory Access
checks.description: /dev/mem or /dev/kmem exposed - allows raw memory read/write!
checks.remediation: Remove /dev/mem and /dev/kmem by disabling CONFIG_DEVMEM and CONFIG_DEVKMEM in the kernel.

checks.label: Block Devices Writable
checks.remediation: Set block device permissions to root-only (chmod 600) to prevent unauthorized disk access.

checks.label: USB-C Port Roles and Power Delivery
checks.command: P=$(ls -d /sys/class/typec/port* 2>/dev/null | head -4); if [ -z "$P" ]; then echo NO_TYPEC_SYSFS; else O=''; for d in $P; do r=$(cat $d/data_role 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\n'); p=$(cat $d/power_role 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\n'); O="$O $(basename $d):data=${r:-?},power=${p:-?}"; done; echo "TYPEC_PRESENT$O"; fi
checks.description: Reports the USB-C port data and power roles. A port in dual-role or host mode negotiates Power Delivery with whatever is attached, and the PD message parser runs in the USB-C controller firmware below the operating system, which is the surface behind the BadPower class of attacks where a malicious charger rewrites controller firmware. A port acting as host also enumerates attacker-supplied devices, reaching every USB class driver in the kernel. Informational because dual-role is the normal configuration on a phone; on a fixed-function device it is often unnecessary.
checks.remediation: On a POS terminal, kiosk or embedded device that only charges, pin the port to sink and device role so it neither sources power nor enumerates attached peripherals, and disable USB host mode in the kernel configuration.
